hlido_opinion.headline: An Apache-2.0, AWS-backed full-stack framework that unifies infrastructure and runtime with end-to-end TypeScript type safety — credible, but explicitly a Preview with 77 open issues.
hlido_opinion.body: AWS Blocks is a well-scoped developer framework: define AWS infrastructure and runtime code together, get end-to-end TypeScript type safety, local mocking, and native client codegen for Kotlin, Swift and Dart. The repo surface is clean — Apache-2.0, TypeScript, CI present, install documented, published to npm, and actively pushed. Two honest cautions keep it at STEADY rather than higher: the project labels itself a Preview, and it carries 77 open issues against 358 stars, which reads as early, in-flux surface area rather than a settled 1.0. There are also no tagged releases yet. For teams already standardized on AWS and TypeScript it is worth a serious look; just budget for churn while it stabilizes. Repo-surface read; we did not build an app with it hands-on.

tier_rationale: STEADY (82, repo-surface ceiling). Apache-2.0, TypeScript with CI, documented install, npm distribution and an AWS-affiliated org clear STEADY comfortably. VITAL is withheld because the project self-describes as a Preview, has no tagged releases, and functional quality cannot be verified from repo signals.
what_it_does_well: Unifies infrastructure-as-code and runtime code with end-to-end TypeScript type safety
Native client codegen for Kotlin, Swift and Dart — real mobile/full-stack reach
Apache-2.0, CI present, documented install, published to npm
Backed by an AWS dev-tools org, targeting a concrete, popular platform
what_it_fails_at: Explicitly a Preview — API stability not yet promised
77 open issues against 358 stars signals early, in-flux surface area
No tagged releases to pin against
Not consumable as a standalone agent interface (agent_consumable did not pass)
best_for: Teams already standardized on AWS and TypeScript
Full-stack apps that need typed infrastructure plus native mobile clients
Developers comfortable adopting a fast-moving Preview framework
not_recommended_for: Teams needing a stable, versioned API today
Agent pipelines wanting a programmatic interface rather than a build-time framework
red_flags: Self-labelled Preview with no tagged releases — expect breaking changes

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A build-time developer framework and SDK for AWS apps; consumed by developers (and agent code-generation) at author time rather than driven as a runtime agent API. No hands-on behavioral test performed.
